title: candidate-feedback-draft-jordan-sanchez-2026-02-27
content:
Candidate: Jordan Sanchez
Role: Senior Backend Engineer (Serving Runtime) — on-site loop notes and early recommendation draft
Interviewer(s): Priya Desai (hiring mgr), Evan Li (runtime), Sofia Martins (sre)
Date(s): phone screen 2026-02-20, take-home 2026-02-22, onsite 2026-02-26

Quick summary / gut: Strong systems thinker, clear communicator, good tradeoff judgement on latency vs cost. Missing hands-on depth in GPU kernel/quantization specifics we care about for the serving runtime. Would be a solid addition to infra/runtime team but may need ramp on model execution internals. 

Detailed notes (raw, still messy):
- Communication: 4/5. Very clear, structured. Used diagrams during system design (drawn on whiteboard) and explained rationale for choices. Good at surfacing constraints early (SLOs, cost targets, expected QPS).
- Coding: 3.5/5. Completed coding exercise (onsite algorithm task) correctly but took a bit longer than expected; code was readable, tests basic. Gave reasonable optimizations (early exits, streaming parser) but missed an edge-case in concurrent buffering (not locking one early pop).
- System design: 4.5/5. Great approach to batching + KV cache layer. Proposed: front-door router -> request dedupe -> adaptive batching service -> KV cache per model variant -> worker pool with model shards. Suggested using consistent hashing for sticky KV-cache locality (like we use), and explained fallback to lower-precision quantized model when latency SLOs are missed.
  - Likes: concrete tradeoffs, quantified latency impact of batching windows, mentioned p99 vs median differences and tail mitigation (prioritization, head-of-line blocking avoidance).
  - Concerns: recommended a custom shard rebalancer that might be complex; didn't discuss rate of rebalancing impact on KV cache cold-starts in depth.
- Product sense / customer focus: 4/5. Asks questions about operational pain (flywheel: dev debugging, traceability). Suggested hooks for tracing tokens and mapping to routes — aligns with Redwood's console needs.
- Domain depth (model exec / GPU): 3/5. Has production experience with CPU-based microservices and some exposure to GPU infra (deployed TF serving cluster at previous company). However, has limited low-level experience with optimized attention kernels, quantized int8 execution, CUDA profiling workflows. Will need mentorship to own kernel selection/quantization optimization work.
- Reliability & ops: 4/5. Strong on autoscaling, SLO-driven routing, can design circuit-breakers and graceful degradation. Nice suggestion to add model-variant scorecards tied to eval sets (we already do this in Optimize).

Specific examples / quotes: "We should measure per-prefix hit rate and let caching policy be keyed by route and model version — otherwise you get weird cross-tenant pollution." Good practical point.

Take-home assignment notes: implemented dedupe + batching simulator, ran microbenchmarks (latency histograms attached in take-home). Results looked plausible. Implementation used Go channels; concurrency was mostly correct but had one race condition when canceling inflight batches (I pointed it out during review).

Red flags / things to validate:
- Verify depth of experience with quantized model variants and if they can lead kernel-level perf troubleshooting. They have theoretical knowledge but limited applied debugging with nvprof/nsight, Triton kernel logs, etc.
- Check willingness / interest to pair on lower-level perf work (they preferred infra design and orchestration over kernel hacking).
- Cultural fit: seems collaborative, open to feedback. Wants mentorship and cares about learning.

Recommendation (draft): Strong hire for a role focused on serving/runtime that splits responsibilities between orchestration + infra design. If we need immediate deep kernel/quantization expertise (owner of kernel selection), this candidate is a medium hire — would require pairing with someone senior in model execution. Tentative: recommend hire for SRE/infra hybrid role on eng-serving-runtime, title Senior Backend Engineer, with a 3-6 month plan to ramp into model-execution tasks.

Proposed interview scorecard (subjective):
- Communication: 4
- Technical breadth (systems): 4
- Technical depth (model exec): 3
- Coding: 3.5
- Ops & reliability: 4
- Hire decision: HIRE (with caveat: needs kernel mentorship)

Next steps / TODOs before final feedback form:
- Evan to add notes from perf follow-up question (2026-02-28).
- Ask Jordan for links to any kernel/profiling artifacts they may have (if they listed them on resume). Quick check: any public repos showing CUDA / Triton work?
- Recruiter to run salary expectation check and relocation timeline (if required).
- Draft final feedback for Greenhouse (JIRA HIR-1243) once we align.

Misc (notes to self):
- Good candidate for owning request routing, adaptive batching, and rollout policies. Could pair on Optimize features (cache scoring).
- If hire, set 90-day goals: 1) pair on model variant perf triage, 2) own one rollout policy (canary -> A/B), 3) implement tracing hook for token-level debugging.

Links / refs: see take-home artifact in GH PR #998; Confluence summary CONFLUENCE-ENG-4567; slack convo thread link above.

End of draft. Will tidy for Greenhouse form after Evan's + Sofia's quick comments.
